readerJob: If ChatGPT can build a dashboard from my company data, what should I trust and check before I use it? Understand how connected sources, company definitions and permissions shape the answer, and know what to verify before sharing or acting on it.

The useful change is that a colleague can ask a business question in ordinary language and receive a dashboard without first writing a database query. The plain question does not remove the machinery underneath it.

The agent can only work with the sources its administrators connect and the records its account is already allowed to see. A permission means which tables, rows and columns the connected account is allowed to see. It interprets those records using a metric definition: the rule a company uses to decide what a number includes.

Imagine asking for active customers. One team may count anyone who logged in this week; another may count people who bought something this month. Both dashboards can look polished and still answer different questions. A missing region in the account's permissions can change the total again. Permissions help limit access; they do not prove the source is complete, the definition is right for this decision or the agent's explanation of a change is correct.

OpenAI released a Data agent in ChatGPT Work on September 10. It is a workplace data tool that can connect an approved ChatGPT Work account to company data, investigate a question and build a dashboard. A colleague can ask why sales slowed or where spending rose without first writing a database query.

OpenAI says the agent can use approved data warehouses, business-intelligence dashboards and files in Google Drive or SharePoint. It can also recommend next steps, share findings through Slack or email and carry out actions through connected tools when the user approves them.

Availability depends on the workplace setup. The Data plugin appears in ChatGPT Work, where administrators install it, configure its data sources and decide who may use them. OpenAI announced no standalone price for the plugin. That does not settle the cost of ChatGPT Work, the connected data services or any other tools a company needs.

The largest evidence gap is accuracy. VentureBeat asked OpenAI for a retrieval or correctness benchmark for the external product and reported that none has been published. OpenAI described an internal comparison with its own data tools but supplied no public number. There is no independent hands-on benchmark yet showing how reliably the product answers questions across customers' systems.

Before sharing a Data agent result, open the evidence behind its findings. Name the source and date, state the metric definition, and compare one important figure with the trusted report your team already uses. If the totals differ, stop at the difference instead of choosing the more convenient number.

Keep the action boundary separate from the analysis. OpenAI's current controls distinguish who can use a plugin, which read or write actions it may take and when ChatGPT asks for approval. For an early test, let the agent prepare the dashboard while sending email, posting to Slack or changing a record still requires a person's approval.

OpenAI says business-product data is not used to train its models by default. Your organization still has to check its exact account, retention requirements, connected-source permissions and workplace policy before adding sensitive data.

The better question is not simply, “Can it make a dashboard?” Ask: “Which data and definition produced this answer, and what happens if it is wrong?”
